newsitem.title: CZECH REPUBLIC: Chemapol plans Czech rights issue, delays GDRs.
newsitem.headline: Chemapol plans Czech rights issue, delays GDRs.

text.p: The rapidly-growing Czech chemicals and industrial conglomerate Chemapol Group a.s. said on Friday it would dalay an international share issue because demand for its stock was so strong at home.

The company said it planned to launch a domestic rights issue to expand equity by 500 million to 800 million crowns (($18.78 million to $30.04 million), and would delay its first planned tranche of global depositary receipts (GDRs) which was expected to be approved on Friday.
Acting spokeswoman Jirina Calfova said a planned extraordinary shareholders' meeting was postponed so the company could put the rights issue to a vote at a general meeting in late October.
She said a previously planned GDR issue of a minimum 600 million crowns would be considered at a later shareholders' meeting in early 1997.

"The main reason (for postponing today's EGM) was continuing strong interest from current shareholders and domestic investors to get shares of our company, and therefore we preferred a domestic issue," Calfova said.

She said the domestic issue was planned to be structured in two rounds with unsubscribed shares carried over as a public offering in a second round. Cheampol Group's current basic equity totals 1.68 billion crowns.

Calfova, who serves as board secretary, also said the closely-held company has applied for its first listing on the Prague Stock Exchange. The initial listing would be on the bourse's so-called free market, not its main market.

Shares in the group -- which controlled, at last count in August, 67 chemical, industrial, trading and media companies -- last traded on Thursday at 2,300 crowns, up 44 crowns on the over-the-counter Czech RM-System where liquidity is negligible.
The group reported consolidated unaudited net profit for the first half of this year of 290 million crowns after audited net profit of 62.5 million crowns in 1995. ($1=26.63 Czech Crown)
